title: rung-4-lifts-for-an-answered-question
intention: Rung 4 of the reseal door lifts for an answered question: `cairn test --reseal --ruling <id>` accepts the id of a question in CairnCommons/questions/ that is resolved and answered by Akien (answered_by begins 'Akien'), as well as a CONFIRMED legacy ruling in CairnCommons/decisions/, so a proof whose claim must change can be reproven under his recorded answer.
why: a proof whose claim must change can be reproven only under a ruling, and rulings were retired 2026-09-14, so rung 4 is unreachable
traces_to: Law 9 (his head says what SHOULD BE; a spec change is his) and Law 8 (a proof that cannot be repaired under his answer leaves its component red forever, so every peer leaning on it stops trusting it); CLAUDE.md 'a deterministic red is fixed, or it carries a decision from Akien ... the decision is an answered question'; RULE 1 (the question tool's public_interface is cairn.tools.question.question); parent 8e3474a6ae43, whose children reshape proofs across components.
how: Measured 2026-10-02: cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py ruling_refusal() reads only cairn.machines.ruling.load_all() — 83 records in CairnCommons/decisions/, 69 confirmed, newest 2026-09-13-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door. Since ticket 9adc6fddf185 (2026-09-14) a decision is an answered question and `cairn ruling open` refuses, so no new id can ever satisfy rung 4: zero seals in the repo carry evidence.reseal_ruling. The door is unreachable for every decision made after 09-13. The fix: ruling_refusal(id) asks cairn.tools.question.question.read(id) (that tool's declared public_interface) when the id carries the question prefix; None when resolved and answered_by starts with 'Akien'; a sentence naming the lack otherwise (open, answered by a measurement, unknown id). A legacy confirmed ruling id still lifts it (decisions/ stays read-only and citable). An answer by measurement does NOT lift rung 4: 'the proof's claim no longer matches the spec' is a spec question, and the spec is his head.
falsifier: RED if: (1) ruling_refusal returns a refusal for a resolved question answered by Akien; (2) it returns None for an open question, for a question answered by a measurement, or for an id that resolves to nothing; (3) a confirmed legacy ruling id no longer lifts rung 4. Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because the reseal door (cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py) runs from the git pre-commit hook every time a proof's closure is staged; a regression shows as a refused rung-4 reseal printed by that hook, so no runtime behaviour is left for a probe to watch
children: none, because the edit is one function (ruling_refusal) in cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py plus one proof
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py, ruling_refusal(ruling_id). (2) What? if the id starts with 'open-', read it through `from cairn.tools.question import question` (question.read); refuse unless record['resolved'] and str(record['answered_by']).startswith('Akien'), each lack in its own sentence; otherwise fall through to the existing ruling-store lookup unchanged. (3) Proof? cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_lifts_for_an_answered_question.py, PROVES keys 1, 2, 3 matching the falsifier clauses, red first, using question records in a scratch root.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient 9c1a0a8cefa7 .. validate 0eda82770902, each learned)

decisions.text: BUILD in cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py: change the signature to ruling_refusal(ruling_id: str, *, question_root: Path | None = None) -> str | None. After the empty-id check, if ruling_id.startswith('open-'): lazily import 'from cairn.tools.question import question as question_mod' (its charter public_interface is cairn.tools.question.question; read(qid, root=None) at question.py:146 returns the record dict and raises question_mod.Refused when the file is absent); call question_mod.read(ruling_id, root=question_root); on Refused return a sentence naming the id and saying no such question exists; if not record.get('resolved') return a sentence naming the id and saying the question is still open; if not str(record.get('answered_by') or '').startswith('Akien') return a sentence naming the id and saying it was answered by a measurement or someone other than Akien, and a spec change is his; else return None. Every other id falls through to the existing ruling_mod.load_all() loop, byte-for-byte unchanged. Update the docstring to name both stores.

PROOF already written and committed red at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_lifts_for_an_answered_question.py (commit dd8596f8): it writes fixture question JSON files (the record shape question.answer writes: id, resolved, answered_by, ...) directly into scratch_dir('cairn-rung4-') and passes that directory as question_root=, so question.read(id, root=question_root) finds them and the live CairnCommons/questions/ is never read; no env var. PROVES 37ddc47686c2 keys 1, 2, 3 = the three teeth. Run: python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_lifts_for_an_answered_question.py; it reads 3 failed before the build (TypeError on question_root) and must read 3 passed after.

NO other file changes: cairn/tools/question/question.py is used through its declared module cairn.tools.question.question and not edited; cairn/machines/ruling is read-only. After the build: seal with 'cairn test --netns --seal --timeout 600 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_lifts_for_an_answered_question.py', then 'cairn test --reseal --timeout 900 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_reseal_door.py' (its rung-4 tooth calls ruling_refusal with one positional argument, which still works).

Measured 2026-10-02 at cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py:181-204: ruling_refusal today does 'from cairn.machines.ruling import ruling as ruling_mod', then 'if not (ruling_id or "").strip(): return "no ruling id was given"', then loops ruling_mod.load_all() matching record['id'] (NOT CONFIRMED sentence / None), then returns the 'no ruling ... in store_dir()' sentence. The question branch goes between the empty-id check and that loop.
